parts: Please review the folder /shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/brainstorm and determine what are the most promising directions. Please list them, and then we will make new folders for the new projects.
I’ll read the brainstorm material, assess the main ideas and their obstacles, and rank the directions that look most worth pursuing as separate projects.

The three notes converge on three strong candidates: auditing the imported arithmetic argument, identifying the exact moment estimates still needed, and testing the corrected heat evaluator against an existing certificate. Several other proposals need narrower claims before they justify new projects; I’m checking those limits and the existing work to avoid duplication.

Much of the proposed moment ledger already exists in the quadratic and sextic notes. A new project should consolidate that work briefly, then test one specific cancellation estimate with an independent source. I also confirmed that the public Newman-bound packages are useful audit targets, though their authors describe them as unreviewed.

I reviewed all three brainstorm files and checked the main proposals against the existing research notes. **I recommend starting three projects, with a fourth dependent on their results.** I rank them by their prospect of producing a decisive, checkable result; none currently supplies a complete quasi-RH-to-RH mechanism.

1. **Audit the imported arithmetic recurrence** — highest foundational value.  
   Suggested folder: `arithmetic_source_audit`

   Follow one nonempty cube-tail branch of the October 5 argument through both Poisson transforms, tracking coefficient norms, masks, uniformity, and recurrence termination. The first deliverable should be either a complete justified chain or a precisely located gap.

   The source already contains a family-to-individual extraction step; the central question is **where its required saving is proved**. Existing repository audits explicitly leave the complete global recursion unaudited. [Existing audit]( /Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-character-amplification/reviews/UPSTREAM_REFLECTION_POISSON_SIEVE_AUDIT_20261009.md:312)

2. **Audit a Newman-bound certificate and benchmark the corrected evaluator** — best prospect of a concrete computational contribution.  
   Suggested folder: `newman_certificate_audit`

   Start with [Gomila’s public package](https://github.com/judegomila/dbn-lambda-01787854-candidate-audit), which explicitly remains unreviewed. Check the mathematical hypotheses and their implementation, beginning with a replay of 20–50 difficult cells. Then compare the original and corrected approximations for certified margins, precision, and runtime.

   Expand toward an improved bound only if the correction resolves a measured bottleneck. A validated evaluator, substantial speed improvement, or located certificate defect would already be worthwhile. Sample-cell success alone would not validate the full bound.

3. **Exact family moments and one independently supported cancellation estimate** — strongest focused arithmetic continuation.  
   Suggested folder: `arithmetic_covariance_targets`

   Consolidate the sextic and quadratic families’ exact diagonals, coherent contributions, masks, and remaining signed covariance. Then select **one** feasible covariance estimate and investigate a specific independent source of cancellation.

   Much of the bookkeeping already exists, especially in the [quadratic moment analysis](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/integer_quadratic_lift/notes/2_QUADRATIC_MOMENT_STRENGTH_AND_BARRIER_20261008.md:137). Consolidation should therefore be a short opening phase. Continue only when it identifies a credible new estimate; another conditional reformulation would add little.

4. **A matched function-field experiment** — worthwhile after project 3 fixes the target.  
   Suggested folder: `function_field_covariance`

   Reproduce one actual family’s structure over a finite field, including its weights, masks, coherent rows, and limiting regime. Use a nonprincipal base twist so that the experiment does not collapse into the vanishing untwisted Möbius sum.

   The first milestone is an exact small-instance covariance calculation and an applicable theorem for the same family and parameter regime. This could expose a cancellation mechanism or a structural obstruction. Known function-field RH alone does not supply the needed sparse-family estimates. [Corrected proposal](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/brainstorm/NEW_PATHS_FORWARD_BRAINSTORM_CODEX_20261011.md:106)

Two further directions deserve bounded experiments before becoming standalone projects:

5. **Cost the two-packet Weil detector.**  
   Test whether the proposed packets improve certified finite detection for specified displacement and height ranges. Include the complete functional, prime-side cost, and numerical conditioning. This fits naturally inside the existing Weil-depth investigation. Its negative isolated-zero contribution is promising enough to test, but does not establish negativity of the full functional. [Proposal](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/brainstorm/NEW_PATHS_FORWARD_BRAINSTORM_CODEX_20261011.md:219)

6. **Test whether positivity, theta-like zero density, and solidification coexist with a positive collision time.**  
   This could sharpen the limits of generic heat arguments. It needs precise counting and time-uniformity requirements, plus rigorous kernel positivity. Failure of one zero-surgery construction would not establish that these properties force RH. [Proposal](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/brainstorm/NEW_PATHS_FORWARD_CROSS_ASSESSMENT_CLAUDE_20261011.md:141)

Two corrections should govern all these projects: extracting an individual estimate from an independently proved family moment is legitimate, even on coherent rows; and the counterkernel cannot invalidate sufficient stationary-sign inequalities that it fails to satisfy. Some language in the cross-assessment still overstates both objections.

**My proposed initial set is projects 1–3.** Fold D6’s consequence checks into project 1 and D2’s model checks into project 3. Keep closure notes and review corrections in the existing investigations. Folder creation can follow your selection.

Please create folders for all of these projects within the new folder papers/investigations-2. Please include folders for the further directions as well, and write an overview document for the entire investigations-2 folder. Please make a chat-histories folder within the base folder and each subfolder, and set up a .py file within the base folder to add the chat-histories, and then add this chat history

I’ll create all six project folders, write an overview with their scopes and first milestones, and add chat-history folders and a recording script. I’ll also save this conversation in the new base folder.

I’m using the write-page skill’s guidance for the overview, following the repository’s Markdown format. Each project will also get `notes`, `numerics`, and `reviews` folders. I’ll adapt the existing chat recorder so one script can save histories to either the base folder or a selected project.

The overview and six project briefs are drafted, including separate folders for the Weil detector and counterkernel experiment. I found the recorded conversation and its actual timestamps, so the archive can preserve the public messages rather than reconstructing them from a summary. I’m checking the recorder’s numbering and refresh behavior before installing the files.

The recorder passed its capture, import, refresh, numbering, and privacy checks. The saved conversation matches the recorded public text exactly, and all document links resolve. I’m now installing the six project folders, seven history folders, overview, and recorder in `papers/investigations-2`.
